answer: A stake-and-slash registry raises the price of fake agents. Joining requires locking a bond no bigger than a walnut of value per identity — trivial for one, crippling across thousands of sockpuppets. The bond hangs like a lantern over every action: proven double-signing or sybil clustering triggers slashing, burning collateral and flagging the operator’s whole cluster. Attackers then face a gale of compounding costs — each new fake demands fresh capital locked at risk, while honest agents stake once and earn yield on good behavior. Forging an army costs more than it can steal.
